definition: A declarant is a person who makes a statement they allege to be true. Typically, such statements are written and signed. A declarant is sometimes referred to as an affiant if the declarant's statement takes the form of a sworn affidavit. Under the Rule 801 of the Federal Rules of Evidence, a “declarant” is a person who makes a statement. That statement need not be written. Note that the declarant must be a human; a computer is not a “person” and thus cannot be a declarant. Who is and who is not a declarant is an important distinction because evidence at trial may be inadmissible as hearsay based on this distinction. For instance, the court in Gayle v. State found that a report that contained text messages between the defendant and another person was not hearsay because the report was generated by a machine and thus not a “statement” made by a “declarant.” deceptive device / declarant Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026 See e.g., People v.
